answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the signal schedule in the raven ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the wander checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 183 aliases therefore means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale.
